rationale: This is essentially the product of two canonical published anomalies (operating profitability and Sloan balance-sheet accruals) with no novel conditioning mechanism, and the IND_RANK(IND_ADJ(...)) double industry normalization is redundant, making the profitability leg a near-monotone transform of itself.

The trend-in-accruals conditioning leg is a defensible earnings-quality deterioration measure and the sign convention is internally consistent (profitability enters only as a magnitude scaler), though it remains a close relative of the archive's accrual-gated profitability signal and the 3-period TREND on differenced balance-sheet items will be noisy.

Up to a symmetric winsorization, IND_ZSCORE of the negated ratio equals minus the archive's leg, so with the expected sign also flipped this is the identical already-tested "Gross Profit Collection Quality" signal (fmb_tstat 0.65) relabeled rather than a new hypothesis.

The conditioning variable is economically thin and arguably signed backwards — rising taxes payable often reflects genuinely high current taxable income, which the tax-based earnings-quality literature treats as confirming rather than contaminating reported profits — and Δtxp is already a component of the working-capital accrual measures used elsewhere in this batch.

This is proposal 1 with R&D added back to the numerator, i.e., a cosmetic variant layering a second known adjustment (intangible-adjusted profitability) onto the same accruals interaction, and COALESCE(xrd,0) additionally conflates true zero R&D with non-reporters.

Conditioning smoothed profitability on both the level and the volatility of accruals is the most substantively differentiated idea in the batch and internally coherent, but the 3-period VOL of twice-differenced balance-sheet items will be noisy and the stacked lag requirements risk pushing coverage below the archive's already thin ~10%.
